_readme: Add a series by adding an entry here — no new script needed.
Run one source:  MODE=discover python scripts/fetch.py NAME   (dump real structure first)
Providers: fred (any FRED id) | eurostat (any dataset+params) | owid (any grapher slug) | csv (any URL) | yahoo (prices) | yahoo_valuation (multiples; Yahoo 429s Actions IPs — may fail)
Everything runs in GitHub Actions — the dev sandbox cannot reach these hosts.

sources.name: cattle-herd
sources.source: FAOSTAT cattle stocks (head), via Our World in Data
sources.note: annual; national totals, all cattle

sources.name: us-prices
sources.source: BLS producer price indexes via FRED, plus CPI for deflating
sources.note: PPI levels are index numbers (1982=100) — ratios only, never quantities
sources.unit: index, 1982 = 100 for producer prices and 1982-84 = 100 for the CPI

sources.name: eu-vet-expenses
sources.source: Eurostat Economic Accounts for Agriculture, veterinary expenses
sources.note: ALL livestock, not cattle only — do not present as a per-cattle figure without saying so

sources.name: eu-hicp
sources.source: Euro area HICP via FRED — deflator for any EUR money series

sources.name: us-cowcalf-costs
sources.source: USDA ERS commodity costs and returns, cow-calf
sources.note: SURVEY BASIS CHANGED IN 2008 — do not compare across that break. Stated per bred cow, except the production block (calves weaned, calves sold, stockers sold, cows calving, beef cows on farm), which counts head per 100 cows, so never sum or average it against the dollar rows.

units.Calves weaned: calves weaned per 100 cows — the weaning percentage
units.Beef cows on farm or ranch: beef cows per 100 cows in the herd, not a cost
units.Cows and heifers calving: cows and heifers calving per 100 cows — the calving percentage

sources.name: eu-herd-countries
sources.source: FAOSTAT cattle stocks (head) by EU member state, via Our World in Data
sources.note: dairy and beef combined, same limitation as the aggregate

sources.name: eu-vet-countries
sources.source: Eurostat EAA veterinary expenses by member state, million EUR, ALL livestock
sources.note: all livestock, not cattle only

sources.name: pharma-gva
sources.source: Eurostat national accounts A*64 — gross value added of NACE C21 (basic pharmaceutical products and preparations), current prices, million national currency
sources.note: NATIONAL CURRENCY on purpose — the pharma/GDP ratio must not carry exchange-rate noise. C21 is manufacturing only: it excludes pharma wholesale, retail pharmacy and R&D services.

sources.name: gdp-total
sources.source: Eurostat national accounts — GDP at market prices, current prices, million national currency
sources.note: same vintage and currency basis as pharma-gva, so the ratio is internally consistent

sources.name: gva-total
sources.source: Eurostat national accounts A*64 — total gross value added, current prices, million national currency
sources.note: the like-for-like denominator. GDP = GVA + taxes less subsidies on products, so pharma/GVA is the cleaner share; pharma/GDP is the more quotable one.

sources.name: manuf-gva
sources.source: Eurostat national accounts A*64 — total manufacturing (NACE C) gross value added, current prices, million national currency
sources.note: context denominator: pharma's share of manufacturing, not just of the whole economy

sources.name: gdp-eur
sources.source: Eurostat national accounts — GDP at market prices, current prices, million EUR
sources.note: for comparing economy SIZE across countries only; never use for the share ratio

sources.name: pharma-gva-eur
sources.source: Eurostat national accounts A*64 — NACE C21 gross value added, current prices, million EUR
sources.note: for comparing absolute pharma output across countries; the share ratio uses the MNAC pair

sources.name: stan-pharma
sources.source: OECD STAN — value added of ISIC C21 (pharmaceuticals), current prices, million national currency
sources.note: same industry definition as NACE C21, so shares are comparable with the Eurostat set; national currency so the ratio carries no FX noise

sources.name: stan-total
sources.source: OECD STAN — total-economy value added, current prices, million national currency
sources.note: denominator for the STAN pharma share; same source and basis as stan-pharma so the ratio is internally consistent

sources.name: pharma-exports
sources.source: Eurostat Comext DS-045409 — exports to world, EUR, by HS4: 3002 immunologicals/vaccines, 3003 bulk medicaments, 3004 dosage medicaments, 2937 hormones, 2941 antibiotics
sources.note: EXPORTS, not production — the product-mix proxy; say so wherever shown

sources.name: pharma-mirror
sources.source: Eurostat Comext DS-045409 — EU27 imports by partner and HS4, EUR: what non-EU producers ship into the EU
sources.note: MIRROR data: reveals a country's export mix to the EU only, not its global mix or production

sources.name: glp1-stocks
sources.source: Yahoo Finance monthly adjusted closes, US listings/ADRs (USD); ^GSPC = S&P 500 index, XBI = SPDR biotech ETF benchmark
sources.note: Adjusted close = split- and dividend-adjusted (total return); index SPX is raw level. ADRs (NVO, AZN, RHHBY, ZLDPF) embed FX moves. Metsera (MTSR) excluded: acquired by Pfizer Nov 2025, delisted — survivorship caveat. Zealand only trades OTC in the US (ZLDPF, thin); primary listing is Copenhagen.
sources.unit: USD per share, except ^GSPC and XBI which are index points

sources.name: valuation-multiples
sources.source: Yahoo Finance quoteSummary — trailing/forward EPS and PE, consensus EPS by horizon, growth rates
sources.note: SNAPSHOT, not a time series: values are as-of the fetch date and are overwritten each run. Forward PE uses next-fiscal-year consensus EPS, so it moves with estimate revisions as well as price. PEG is computed as forward PE / expected EPS growth — Yahoo's own pegRatio field is unreliable. Loss-making companies have no meaningful PE: those cells are intentionally blank. SpaceX is private and has no multiples at all.
sources.unit: USD per share for EPS, a ratio for PE, percent for growth

sources.name: hs6-check
sources.source: HS6 detail by reporter — establishes where detailed codes are published vs suppressed
sources.unit: trade value in EUR; this file is a probe of what the source publishes, not a series to quote

sources.name: pharma-dest
sources.source: Destination markets for the concentration leaders, by HS4 class, 2024

sources.name: pharma-hs6-trend
sources.source: Eurostat Comext DS-045409 — exports to world by HS6 therapeutic class, 2010-2024
sources.note: 293719 polypeptide hormones (GLP-1/insulin-analogue class, bulk); 300241 human vaccines; 300215 immunological in doses (antibodies); 300212 antisera/blood fractions; 300431 insulin medicaments; 300439 other hormone medicaments; 300490 other medicaments

sources.name: peptide-flows
sources.source: Comext — HS 2937.19 imports (flow 1) and exports (flow 2), value and quantity
sources.note: net exports test: re-export shows as large imports; domestic production does not

units.BE|1|QUANTITY_IN_100KG: hundreds of kilograms, as Comext publishes it — multiply by 100 for kg
units.BE|2|QUANTITY_IN_100KG: hundreds of kilograms, as Comext publishes it — multiply by 100 for kg
units.DE|1|QUANTITY_IN_100KG: hundreds of kilograms, as Comext publishes it — multiply by 100 for kg
units.DE|2|QUANTITY_IN_100KG: hundreds of kilograms, as Comext publishes it — multiply by 100 for kg
units.DK|1|QUANTITY_IN_100KG: hundreds of kilograms, as Comext publishes it — multiply by 100 for kg
units.DK|2|QUANTITY_IN_100KG: hundreds of kilograms, as Comext publishes it — multiply by 100 for kg
units.FR|1|QUANTITY_IN_100KG: hundreds of kilograms, as Comext publishes it — multiply by 100 for kg
units.FR|2|QUANTITY_IN_100KG: hundreds of kilograms, as Comext publishes it — multiply by 100 for kg
units.IE|1|QUANTITY_IN_100KG: hundreds of kilograms, as Comext publishes it — multiply by 100 for kg
units.IE|2|QUANTITY_IN_100KG: hundreds of kilograms, as Comext publishes it — multiply by 100 for kg
units.IT|1|QUANTITY_IN_100KG: hundreds of kilograms, as Comext publishes it — multiply by 100 for kg
units.IT|2|QUANTITY_IN_100KG: hundreds of kilograms, as Comext publishes it — multiply by 100 for kg

sources.name: peptide-dest
sources.source: Comext — where Ireland's bulk peptide hormone exports go

sources.name: gni-gdp
sources.source: Eurostat nasa_10_nf_tr — gross national income (B5G), total economy
sources.note: GNI minus GDP is net primary income from abroad: negative where foreign-owned profits are repatriated out, positive where a country's firms earn abroad. B5G is a balance, so the PAID and RECV keys carry the same figure; read either

sources.name: fx-eur
sources.source: Eurostat ert_bil_eur_a — annual average exchange rates, national currency per euro
sources.note: used only to express absolute pharma value added in a common currency; every share ratio stays in national currency

sources.name: vet-cpi-eu
sources.source: Eurostat HICP monthly index (2015=100): CP00 all-items, CP0934 pets and related products, CP0935 veterinary and other services for pets
sources.note: CONSUMER prices — pet vet services paid by households, not farm animal health costs. Confirmed by 2026-08 fetch: TR publishes CP00 only (no CP0934/CP0935 — a TR vet series needs TÜİK/EVDS); IE CP0935 stops at 2023-12; all other geos current. Base years differ per country (earliest obs 1996-01 FR, 2016-12 for late joiners) — index everything to a common month before comparing.

sources.name: ppi-eu
sources.source: Eurostat sts_inppd_m — domestic producer prices, monthly, 2021=100, unadjusted: pharma manufacturing (C21), total manufacturing (C), energy supply (D)
sources.note: Feeds the cost-escalation tool. C21 coverage varies by country — missing combos declared in the tool, never guessed. Türkiye included (confirmed by value-level probe 2026-08: full series 2015-01 onward).

sources.name: lci-eu
sources.source: Eurostat lc_lci_r2_q — labour cost index, industry (B-E), quarterly, 2020=100, seasonally and calendar adjusted, total labour cost
sources.note: Feeds the cost-escalation tool. SCA chosen so arbitrary quarter-to-quarter windows are not distorted by bonus seasonality — stated on the tool.

sources.name: fx-eur-m
sources.source: Eurostat ert_bil_eur_m — monthly average exchange rates, national currency per euro
sources.note: Feeds the cost-escalation tool. BGN not published monthly (currency-board peg to EUR) — noted in the tool.

sources.name: food-cpi-eu
sources.source: Eurostat HICP monthly index (2015=100), all food classes CP0111-CP0122 plus CP011 food and CP00 all items, since Dec 2016
sources.note: Feeds the Food Basket Explorer. Ratio metric (class ÷ CP011) computed client-side; sinceTimePeriod trims payload for page load.

sources.name: meat-cpi-eu
sources.source: Eurostat HICP monthly index (2015=100): CP00 all items, CP011 food, CP0112 meat
sources.note: CP0112 'Meat' (COICOP 01.1.2) includes fresh/frozen/processed meat and poultry. TR class-level coverage to be confirmed by the fetch report.

sources.name: meat-cpi-us
sources.source: BLS CPI via FRED, NSA, US city average: SAF112 meats/poultry/fish/eggs, SAF11 food at home, all items
sources.note: US basket differs from EU CP0112: SAF112 includes fish and eggs, and FRED does not carry the narrower SAF1121 (meats, poultry, fish), so the basket difference is stated wherever shown

sources.name: vet-cpi-us
sources.source: BLS CPI via FRED: pet services including veterinary (SS62031, 1997-12→) and all-items — US city average, not seasonally adjusted
sources.note: CONSUMER prices, same object as vet-cpi-eu: EU CP0935 is 'veterinary and OTHER services for pets', so the like-for-like US series is pet services INCLUDING veterinary, not veterinarian services alone (BLS SS62032 exists but is not mirrored on FRED — both CUUR/CUSR ids 404). NSA throughout so the vet/headline ratio is like-for-like.

sources.name: elec-eu
sources.source: Eurostat nrg_pc_205 — electricity, non-household band IC (500–1 999 MWh), excl. recoverable taxes, national currency per kWh, semi-annual
sources.note: Escalation tool: mid-size industrial benchmark band, published since 2007. NAC on purpose — FX is its own factor.
sources.unit: national currency per kWh, excluding recoverable taxes

sources.name: energy-spot
sources.source: Daily and weekly energy spot prices via FRED: Brent (DCOILBRENTEU) and WTI (DCOILWTICO) crude in USD per barrel, Henry Hub natural gas (DHHNGSP) in USD per million BTU, and US average retail regular gasoline (GASREGW) and diesel (GASDESW) in USD per gallon
sources.note: The current price, as against the monthly benchmarks in wb-commodities. Crude and Henry Hub gas are daily from 1986, 1987 and 1997; the two pump prices are weekly from 1990 and 1994. Full dates are kept, so these are the actual quotes rather than a month-end snapshot — resample with frequency='annual_mean' before mixing them with monthly or annual data. Nominal USD, not seasonally adjusted, and the pump prices include federal and state taxes while the crude and gas quotes do not.

sources.name: energy-household-eu
sources.source: Eurostat nrg_pc_204 — electricity prices for household consumers, band DC (2 500–4 999 kWh a year), all taxes and levies included, euro per kWh, semi-annual from 2007
sources.note: What a household actually pays, as against the industrial bands in elec-eu and gas-eu. Taxes included on purpose: the tax wedge is most of what separates one country from another. Euro rather than national currency, so the countries are directly comparable and an exchange-rate move shows up in the price.
sources.unit: EUR per kWh, all taxes included

sources.name: gas-household-eu
sources.source: Eurostat nrg_pc_202 — natural gas prices for household consumers, band D2 (20–199 GJ a year), all taxes and levies included, euro per gigajoule, semi-annual from 2007
sources.note: The household counterpart to gas-eu, which is the industrial band. Taxes included. Countries with no gas network are legitimately absent rather than missing.
sources.unit: EUR per gigajoule, all taxes included

sources.name: gas-eu
sources.source: Eurostat nrg_pc_203 — natural gas, non-household band I3 (10 000–99 999 GJ), excl. recoverable taxes, national currency per GJ, semi-annual
sources.note: Escalation tool: mid-size industrial benchmark band. Countries without gas networks legitimately absent.
sources.unit: national currency per gigajoule, excluding recoverable taxes

sources.name: europe-map
sources.source: Natural Earth 110m admin-0 countries (public domain), filtered to Europe, coordinates rounded
sources.note: Selector map for the escalation dashboard. ISO_A2_EH property (plain ISO_A2 is -99 for FR/NO in NE). GR→EL translated client-side.

sources.name: cpi-eu
sources.source: Eurostat prc_hicp_minr — HICP all items (ECOICOP2), monthly index, 2015=100
sources.note: Feeds the cost-escalation tool's CPI factor. Successor of prc_hicp_midx, which was archived at 2025-12 with the 2026 rebase (ECOICOP2, coicop18 dimension, all-items code TOTAL). meat-cpi-eu kept as the frozen pre-rebase file for the meat post and basket explorer.

sources.name: eu-ppp
sources.source: Eurostat purchasing power parities and price level indices (prc_ppp_ind)
sources.note: Codes pinned from MODE=discover run 2026-08-19. All 55 geos kept (incl. EU/EA aggregates, UK, US, JP, TR, Western Balkans). No veterinary/pharma category exists in this dataset — lowest health detail is A0106/A010603. COICOP 2018 rebase: category-level series may be short or broken around 2021/22 — check spans before charting.
sources.unit: price level index, EU27 = 100, and PPP conversion factors

sources.name: eu-vet-sbs
sources.source: Eurostat SBS annual detailed enterprise statistics for services, veterinary activities (NACE M75)
sources.note: Codes pinned from discover 2026-08-20: V11110 enterprises, V12110 turnover (M EUR), V12150 value added (M EUR), V16110 persons employed, V91100 turnover per person employed (k EUR). 39 geos. Legacy SBS series — check the fetched span; 2021+ lives in the successor EBS dataset (separate hunt).
sources.unit: as published by Eurostat SBS; check the series id for the variable

sources.name: eu-vet-weight
sources.source: Eurostat HICP item weights — share of veterinary and pet services in each country's consumption basket
sources.note: HICP item weights, per-mille of total basket: CP0934 pets and related products, CP0935 veterinary and other services for pets. Dataset serves no 2026 (checked in discover — ECOICOP2 rebase); weights for 2026+ need the successor dataset once Eurostat publishes it. A stored 0 means the country did not collect that item's weight in that year (Kosovo throughout, Iceland to 2021), not a zero share
sources.unit: per mille of the consumption basket

sources.name: bigmac-usd
sources.source: The Economist Big Mac index (open data, github.com/TheEconomist/big-mac-data) — Big Mac price converted to USD at market rates
sources.note: Semi-annual (Jan+Jul), 2000->today; a one-item price level, current within ~6 months — the timeliness complement to Eurostat PPP (annual, ~18-month lag). One burger is not a consumption basket.

sources.name: bigmac-eur
sources.source: The Economist Big Mac index — raw valuation vs the euro (0 = burger costs the same as in the euro area; +0.10 = 10% dearer)
sources.note: Same file as bigmac-usd, euro-relative column; fractions, not percent.
sources.unit: fraction, not percent: -0.17 means a Big Mac is 17% cheaper than in the euro area, +0.28 means 28% dearer. Multiply by 100 before quoting a percentage.

sources.name: bigmac-src-eur
sources.source: The Economist Big Mac index SOURCE data — euro-denominated prices: individual euro members (from 2011-07) plus the EUZ weighted average, in EUR
sources.note: Member prices are The Economist's collected source prices, not headline index rows; parity vs the euro area = member price / EUZ price - 1, computed per edition on the page.

sources.name: pl-ppi-probe
sources.source: PROBE: Eurostat industrial producer prices, domestic market — which NACE codes does Poland actually report? (notes/broiler-parity-poland.md)
sources.note: Discovery helper for the broiler parity build; run with MODE=discover. Tiny time window on purpose so the monthly full fetch stays cheap if it sweeps this.
sources.unit: index; a probe of which NACE codes Poland publishes

sources.name: pl-anchor-out-probe
sources.source: PROBE: Eurostat annual absolute selling prices of animal products — live-chicken price, Poland (parity anchor numerator)
sources.note: MODE=discover first; dataset id itself is a best guess — a 404 here is an answer, not a failure.
sources.unit: PLN; a probe of which price series exist

sources.name: pl-anchor-in-probe
sources.source: PROBE: Eurostat annual absolute purchase prices of the means of production — broiler feed price, Poland (parity anchor denominator)
sources.note: MODE=discover first; dataset id itself is a best guess — a 404 here is an answer, not a failure.
sources.unit: PLN; a probe of which price series exist

sources.name: pl-broiler-ppi
sources.source: Eurostat sts_inppd_m: Poland domestic producer price index, processing & preserving of poultry meat (C1012) and prepared feeds for farm animals (C1091)
sources.note: The Polish leg of the broiler parity — same NACE pair as the TR series (TÜİK C10.12/C10.91). Codes confirmed by the 2026-08 probe (data/_pl-parity-probe.json).

sources.name: pl-anchor-chicken
sources.source: Eurostat annual selling prices: chickens (live, 1st choice), Poland, PLN per 100 kg LIVE weight
sources.note: Parity anchor numerator. LIVE weight — the builder converts to carcass-equivalent with a disclosed yield before anchoring, because the TR anchor (TEPGE) is per kg meat.

sources.name: pl-anchor-feed
sources.source: Eurostat annual purchase prices: complete feed for broiler production (in bulk), Poland, PLN per 100 kg
sources.note: Parity anchor denominator. Product code confirmed by the 2026-08 probe.

sources.name: popular-markets
sources.source: Yahoo Finance monthly closes: Bitcoin (BTC-USD), Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC), S&P 500 (^GSPC), COMEX gold front-month (GC=F)
sources.note: Start 2014-09 = first month Yahoo has BTC-USD. Indices/futures pay no dividends; BTC has none - closes are comparable for co-movement, not total return.
sources.unit: USD for BTC and gold, index points for ^IXIC and ^GSPC

sources.name: climate-co2
sources.source: Atmospheric CO2 concentration (ppm), long-term - Our World in Data grapher co2-long-term-concentration
sources.note: Annual. Run MODE=discover first if the slug or entity name has drifted.

sources.name: climate-temp
sources.source: Global mean temperature anomaly (deg C vs 1861-1890) - Our World in Data grapher temperature-anomaly
sources.note: Annual. Grapher entity may be 'Global' or 'World' depending on vintage - both mapped; keep whichever returns data.

sources.name: pump-vs-oil
sources.source: US city-average retail gasoline price (BLS APU000074714, USD/gallon) and WTI crude spot (MCOILWTICO, USD/barrel), monthly via FRED
sources.note: Gasoline from 1976, WTI from 1986; both nominal USD - the shared-dollar trend is part of the story the checker tells.

sources.name: tr-cpi-ppi
sources.source: TCMB EVDS, TÜİK price indices: CPI general, food, core B and C, services and rent on the 2025=100 base (TP.TUKFIY2025.*, TP.FE25.*), back-cast to 2005; CPI general (TP.FG.J0) and domestic PPI (TP.TUFE1YI.T1) on the 2003=100 base
sources.note: Use 'cpi' (2025=100, from 2005-01) as the deflator. The 2003=100 CPI stops at 2026-01 with the 2026 rebase; the PPI is still published on the 2003 base. Core B excludes unprocessed food, energy, alcohol, tobacco and gold; core C also excludes all food. For annual inflation apply transform=yoy to 'cpi'; the EVDS code once stored here as cpi_yoy (TP.FE.OKTG01) is the 2003=100 index again, not a change

sources.name: tr-rates
sources.source: TCMB EVDS: one-week repo policy rate, weighted average TRY deposit rate up to 3 months, housing and commercial loan rates; monthly averages of weekly data
sources.note: Percent per annum. Monthly average of weekly observations, so a mid-month decision shows as a partial move in that month

sources.name: fao-livestock
sources.source: FAOSTAT QCL: livestock stocks (head) and production of meat, milk and eggs (tonnes), annual
sources.note: Series keys are area|item|element: stocks are head (element 'stock', for the *_stock items), production is tonnes (element 'production', for meat, milk and eggs). FAO figures are official, estimated or imputed by country and year; flags are on the FAOSTAT site
sources.unit: head for stocks, tonnes for production

sources.name: fao-producer-prices
sources.source: FAOSTAT PP: annual producer prices in USD per tonne, farm gate
sources.note: USD/tonne converted by FAO at annual average exchange rates, so a lira devaluation shows as a price fall in USD while local prices rise. Series keys are area|item

sources.name: imf-weo
sources.source: IMF World Economic Outlook via the IMF Data API (latest release), 30 economies: real GDP growth (NGDP_RPCH), inflation average and end-period (PCPIPCH, PCPIEPCH), unemployment (LUR), government gross debt and net lending % GDP (GGXWDG_NGDP, GGXCNL_NGDP), current account % GDP (BCA_NGDPD), GDP per capita and GDP in USD (NGDPDPC, NGDPD), investment and saving % GDP (NID_NGDP, NGSD_NGDP)
sources.note: Series keys are country|indicator. Actuals through the release's last actual year, IMF projections after it (usually five years ahead); the two are not distinguished in the file, so treat the last five or six years as forecasts. Percent for rates, USD (full dollars, not billions) for NGDPD, USD for NGDPDPC

units.NGDP_RPCH: percent change on a year earlier
units.PCPIPCH: percent change on a year earlier, period average
units.PCPIEPCH: percent change on a year earlier, end of period
units.NGDPD: current US dollars (full dollars, not billions)

sources.name: asia-wdi
sources.source: World Bank World Development Indicators via the World Bank API, annual, 20 Asian and Middle Eastern economies plus Türkiye: growth, GDP per capita PPP (constant 2021 international $), GDP in USD billions, CPI inflation, unemployment (ILO modelled), population in millions, exports, manufacturing and agriculture value added as % of GDP, FDI inflows % of GDP, gross capital formation % of GDP, urban share, energy use per capita, R&D % of GDP, high-tech exports % of manufactured exports
sources.note: Series keys are country|indicator. WDI revises history and lags one to two years; the latest year for a country is often missing for slow indicators (energy, R&D). Taiwan is not a World Bank member and returns nothing for most indicators
sources.unit: varies by indicator; the series id names the World Bank code

sources.name: tr-fx-monthly
sources.source: TCMB EVDS indicative buying rates, monthly averages of daily quotes
sources.note: TRY per unit of foreign currency. EVDS serves the pre-2005 history in old lira (1,393,340 per dollar in December 2004); the fetch divides those months by a million so the series is on today's lira throughout
sources.unit: Turkish lira per unit of foreign currency

sources.name: tr-house-prices
sources.source: TCMB Residential Property Price Index (KFE), 2023=100, monthly
sources.note: Nominal index; deflate with tr-cpi-ppi for real house prices

sources.name: wb-commodities
sources.source: World Bank Commodity Price Data (the Pink Sheet), monthly nominal US dollar prices
sources.note: Nominal USD. Units differ by commodity (USD/bbl, USD/mt, USD/kg, USD/troy oz); see the Pink Sheet header. Feed inputs (maize, soybean meal), fertilizers (urea, DAP, potash) and metals are the engineering and chemistry inputs. Woodpulp is not on the monthly sheet; the Pink Sheet publishes it annually only.

units.iron_ore: nominal USD per dry metric ton unit

sources.name: wb-commodity-indices
sources.source: World Bank Commodity Price Data (the Pink Sheet), monthly price indices, 2010 = 100
sources.note: Nominal US dollar price indices with 2010 = 100, so the groups are directly comparable with each other and with the individual prices in wb-commodities once those are rebased. Energy is the crude, gas and coal basket; Non-energy covers agriculture, fertilizers and metals.

sources.name: us-sentiment
sources.source: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers via FRED: sentiment index (1966Q1=100) and median expected 1-year inflation
sources.note: Preliminary readings are revised at month end
sources.unit: index, 1966 Q1 = 100 for sentiment; percent for expected inflation

sources.name: us-ip-sectors
sources.source: Federal Reserve industrial production by NAICS industry via FRED, 2017=100, seasonally adjusted, monthly
sources.note: Chemicals 325, pharmaceuticals 3254, machinery 333, computer and electronic products 334, electrical equipment 335. Index levels, not output volumes

sources.name: us-ppi-sectors
sources.source: BLS producer price indexes by NAICS industry via FRED, not seasonally adjusted, monthly
sources.note: Base periods differ by series (index = 100 at the series start). Ratios and growth rates only
sources.unit: index, as published by BLS; base year varies by series

sources.name: eu-gva-sectors
sources.source: Eurostat national accounts A*64, gross value added at current prices, million EUR: chemicals (C20), computer and electronic (C26), electrical equipment (C27), machinery (C28), motor vehicles (C29)
sources.note: Current prices in EUR, so cross-country levels carry exchange-rate effects; pharma (C21) is in pharma-gva-eur

sources.name: chem-eng-exports
sources.source: Eurostat Comext DS-045409, exports to world, EUR, by HS chapter: 28 inorganic chemicals, 29 organic chemicals, 38 miscellaneous chemical products, 84 machinery, 85 electrical machinery and electronics, 87 vehicles, 90 optical, measuring and medical instruments
sources.note: Customs values; intra-EU flows included in 'world'. Türkiye is not a Comext reporter

sources.name: eu-esi
sources.source: European Commission business and consumer surveys via Eurostat ei_bssi_m_r2, seasonally adjusted, monthly: economic sentiment indicator (long-run mean 100), industrial, consumer and services confidence balances
sources.note: ESI is an index around 100; the confidence indicators are percentage balances around zero. Türkiye is covered by the EC survey programme

units.EU27_2020|BS-ICI-BAL: balance of responses in percentage points (positive minus negative answers), around zero
units.EU27_2020|BS-CSMCI-BAL: balance of responses in percentage points (positive minus negative answers), around zero
units.EU27_2020|BS-SCI-BAL: balance of responses in percentage points (positive minus negative answers), around zero
units.DE|BS-ICI-BAL: balance of responses in percentage points (positive minus negative answers), around zero
units.DE|BS-CSMCI-BAL: balance of responses in percentage points (positive minus negative answers), around zero

sources.name: eu-hpi
sources.source: Eurostat house price index prc_hpi_q, all purchases, quarterly index 2015=100
sources.note: Nominal. Coverage starts later for some countries; Türkiye house prices are in tr-house-prices from TCMB

sources.name: eu-ipi-sectors
sources.source: Eurostat sts_inpr_m industrial production, seasonally and calendar adjusted, 2021=100, monthly: manufacturing (C), chemicals (C20), pharma (C21), computer and electronic (C26), electrical equipment (C27), machinery (C28), motor vehicles (C29)
sources.note: Volume indices. Sector detail is missing for some smaller countries; empty combinations are dropped

sources.name: eu-ppi-sectors
sources.source: Eurostat sts_inppd_m domestic producer prices, unadjusted, 2021=100, monthly: chemicals (C20), computer and electronic (C26), electrical equipment (C27), machinery (C28), motor vehicles (C29)
sources.note: Pharma (C21) and total manufacturing are in ppi-eu

sources.name: eu-berd-sectors
sources.source: Eurostat rd_e_berdindr2 business enterprise R&D expenditure, million EUR, annual: manufacturing (C), chemicals (C20), pharma (C21), computer and electronic (C26), electrical equipment (C27), machinery (C28)
sources.note: Biennial for some countries; latest year is often provisional. Pharma BERD is the closest public proxy for biotech R&D

sources.name: population
sources.source: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, total population, annual, via the World Bank API
sources.note: Series keys are country|population. Mid-year estimates; the World Bank revises history after each census round. EU is the EU27 aggregate. Used to put counts and totals on a per-person basis.

sources.name: central-bank-assets
sources.source: Federal Reserve H.4.1, ECB and Bank of Japan balance sheets via FRED: WALCL, ECBASSETSW, JPNASSETS, WRESBAL, M2SL, CURRCIR
sources.note: Different currencies and units: the Fed and ECB in millions of their own currency, the Bank of Japan in hundred millions of yen, US M2 and currency in billions. Compare shapes or rebase, never levels across banks. The Fed and ECB publish weekly; this file keeps the last observation of each month so everything is monthly

sources.name: tr-cb-balance
sources.source: TCMB analytical balance sheet via EVDS: assets, foreign and domestic assets, foreign liabilities, CBRT money, reserve money, currency issued, banking sector deposits
sources.note: Business-day series in thousand Turkish lira, nominal. The lira has lost most of its value over this window, so deflate with tr-cpi-ppi or read against the exchange rate before comparing years

sources.name: macro-external
sources.source: World Bank World Development Indicators: trade balance, current account, exports and imports, reserves, external debt, broad money, FDI, remittances and the real effective exchange rate, 30 economies
sources.note: Series keys are country|indicator. Annual, and the World Bank lags one to two years; external debt is reported only by low and middle income countries, so it is empty for the advanced economies here. Government debt is not here: the WDI series is central government only and covers a third of these countries in odd years; use imf-weo GGXWDG_NGDP for general government gross debt. Broad money is missing for euro-area members (the ECB reports it for the area) and the REER for Türkiye

sources.name: us-transport
sources.source: US Bureau of Transportation Statistics and BEA via FRED, monthly: Transportation Services Index total (TSITTL), freight (TSIFRGHT) and passenger (TSIPSNGR), vehicle miles travelled (TRFVOLUSM227NFWA), airline revenue passenger miles (AIRRPMTSI), rail freight carloads (RAILFRTCARLOADSD11), total light-vehicle sales (TOTALSA)
sources.note: The three TSI series are seasonally adjusted indices with 2000 = 100; the rest are physical volumes, so compare shapes or use an index. Vehicle miles are not seasonally adjusted and swing with the season; vehicle sales are an annualised monthly rate in millions of units

units.vehicle_miles_m: million vehicle-miles a month, not seasonally adjusted
units.air_rpm_k: thousand revenue passenger miles a month
units.vehicle_sales_m: million units a year, seasonally adjusted annual rate

sources.name: wb-transport
sources.source: World Bank World Development Indicators (ICAO and UNCTAD data), annual: air passengers carried by airlines registered in the country, air freight in million tonne-km, container port traffic in TEU, rail passenger-km and rail freight tonne-km
sources.note: Series keys are country|indicator. Air passengers are counted by the airline's country of registration, not where the flight was: Türkiye's number is largely Turkish Airlines wherever it flies. Rail series stop around 2020-21 in the WDI; air and ports run to 2023-24

sources.name: eu-air-passengers
sources.source: Eurostat avia_paoc: passengers carried, all schedules, by reporting country and coverage (total, international, national), monthly
sources.note: Series keys are country|coverage. Passengers carried counts each passenger once per flight stage at the reporting country's airports; a Frankfurt–Istanbul passenger appears in both Germany's and Türkiye's totals. Türkiye reports from 2017. Not seasonally adjusted: compare a month with the same month a year earlier

sources.name: eu-car-registrations
sources.source: Eurostat road_eqr_carpda: new passenger car registrations by motor energy, annual
sources.note: Series keys are country|fuel: TOTAL all fuels, PET petrol, DIE diesel, ELC battery electric, ELC_PET_HYB petrol hybrid, ELC_PET_PI plug-in petrol hybrid. Divide ELC by TOTAL for the electric share. The hybrid split exists only from 2017 and some countries report it late; the UK stops after 2019

sources.name: electricity-mix
sources.source: Ember Yearly Electricity Data and the Energy Institute Statistical Review, via Our World in Data: electricity generated by source, TWh, annual
sources.note: Series keys are country|source. Generation, not capacity and not consumption: a country that imports power shows less here than it uses. Coal, gas and oil start in 1985 for most countries; the renewables and nuclear columns reach back to 1965. The last year is often Ember's provisional figure

sources.name: renewables-share
sources.source: Ember and the Energy Institute via Our World in Data: share of electricity generated from renewables (hydro, wind, solar, bioenergy, other), annual
sources.note: A share of generation, so a dry year moves a hydro-heavy country (Türkiye, Norway, Brazil) even when nothing was built. Nuclear is not counted as renewable

sources.name: eu-renewables-share
sources.source: Eurostat nrg_ind_ren: share of energy from renewable sources, the official figure behind the EU targets, annual since 2004
sources.note: Series keys are country|measure: REN overall (gross final energy consumption), REN_ELC electricity, REN_TRA transport, REN_HEAT_CL heating and cooling. The Renewable Energy Directive's accounting rules, so the electricity share differs from Ember's generation share in renewables-share. Türkiye is not in this table

sources.name: tr-electricity
sources.source: TEİAŞ daily electricity balance via TCMB EVDS (TP.ELEKTUKETIM.*), summed to calendar months by EVDS: production, consumption, imports and exports
sources.note: EVDS publishes MWh a day; this file holds GWh a month. The current month is left out until it is complete. Consumption exceeds production by roughly the net import; the renewable/non-renewable split in EVDS starts only in 2026 and is not stored

sources.name: eu-tourism-nights
sources.source: Eurostat tour_occ_nim: nights spent at hotels, holiday and short-stay accommodation and campsites, by residents and foreign visitors, monthly
sources.note: Series keys are country|residence: TOTAL, FOR foreign visitors, DOM residents. Nights, not arrivals, and only in registered accommodation: short-term rentals are largely outside it. Türkiye reports from 2018. Strong seasonality: compare year on year or use annual sums

sources.name: tr-tourism-arrivals
sources.source: Ministry of Culture and Tourism border statistics via TCMB EVDS (TP.URISTSAYIL.*): foreign visitors arriving, by province of entry, monthly
sources.note: Arrivals at the border, counted by the province of the crossing: Antalya and Muğla are the resort airports, Edirne the road border from Bulgaria and Greece. Foreign visitors only; Turkish citizens living abroad are not in it. EVDS files the group as an archive but it is still updated

sources.name: ai-investment
sources.source: Stanford AI Index (Quid data) via Our World in Data: private investment in AI companies by region, annual
sources.note: Private investment means venture and private equity deals, not corporate spending on chips and data centres, so hyperscaler capital expenditure is not in it. Europe is Quid's region, not the EU. Nominal US dollars; the 2025 figure is a partial-year count. OWID publishes plain dollars; stored here in billions

sources.name: ai-investment-type
sources.source: Stanford AI Index via Our World in Data: world corporate investment in AI by deal type, annual
sources.note: World totals only. The merger/acquisition line is lumpy: one large deal moves a year. OWID publishes plain dollars; stored here in billions

sources.name: ai-systems
sources.source: Epoch AI via Our World in Data: cumulative number of large-scale AI systems (training compute above 10^23 FLOP) by the country of the developing organisation, annual
sources.note: Cumulative counts, so every line only rises. Country is where the organisation is based; a model trained by a multinational team is under Multinational. Epoch's catalogue is curated, not exhaustive

sources.name: us-chips
sources.source: Federal Reserve industrial production via FRED, monthly, seasonally adjusted: semiconductors and other electronic components (NAICS 3344) and computer and electronic products (NAICS 334)
sources.note: Volume indices, 2017 = 100, and for semiconductors the Fed's quality adjustment makes the index rise with chip performance, not only with units shipped
